problem: vague copy, my copy sounds generic, how to make claims believable, copy not converting, weak offer language
symptom: Offer copy reads 'best quality', 'premium results', 'top photographer' and prospects discount it or do not respond.
technique: Be Specific; Generalities Have Zero Weight (Hopkins Ch 7)
exact_steps: Replace every generality with a tested figure, number, or concrete process detail. Rule: 'Best in the world' = worthless; '9% net profit, here is the actual cost breakdown' wins. Hopkins example: shaving soap that said 'Softens the beard in one minute. Maintains creamy fullness for 10 minutes. Result of 130 tested formulas' destroyed a saturated market. SNIPED application: not 'studio-grade editorial portraits' but '5-pass cull, 5-mask retouch stack, your face/body/skin untouched, delivered in a private gallery in 10 days.' One brewer won by stating the plate-glass cooling room, four-times-washed bottles, 4,000-foot wells, 1,018 yeast experiments (things every brewer did but no one had stated). Audit pass: scan the copy, count generalities, force each one into a specific.
inputs_needed: Draft copy/offer text, real process facts and numbers from the SNIPED pipeline (cull passes, mask count, turnaround days, edit specifics)
output_artifact: Revised copy block where every generality is replaced by a specific claim/figure
when_to_use: Finalizing Carrd copy, Op Kit one-pager, Reset offer description, VIB DM, any sales asset
when_not: When the specific would expose identity-AI use or violate the faceless-safe lock; never invent figures you cannot back

problem: cold dm opener, weak subject line, low reply rate, headline, how to start a pitch, wrong leads responding
symptom: Strong offer but no replies, or replies from the wrong (off-scope, can't-afford) crowd.
technique: The Headline Is Half The Ad / Headline Selects The Reader (Hopkins Ch 5)
exact_steps: Spend more time on the headline/opener than on the body. The headline's only job is to HAIL the exact buyer you want and repel everyone else. A bad headline on a great ad = zero returns; a headline change alone multiplied returns 5x-10x on identical body copy. Rule: never use clever or blind headlines, they attract the wrong crowd and miss the right one. SNIPED application: VIB DM opener and LinkedIn comment opener must name the specific buyer (e.g. 'LA founders raising a round' / 'executives'). Hopkins proved 'offer limited to executives' outperforms the same offer to all because exclusivity selects identity. Always run 2+ headline/opener variants on any significant push.
inputs_needed: Target buyer definition (Tier 0 CRM founder profile), the offer body, 2+ opener variants
output_artifact: 2+ keyed opener/headline variants ready to test, each naming the target buyer
when_to_use: VIB DM, LinkedIn comment opener, email subject line, any first-line of a sales asset
when_not: Never use a clever/blind headline that hides who it is for; do not send any outreach (draft only per lock)

problem: should I scale this offer, risky launch, how to validate an offer, big spend decision, untested campaign
symptom: About to commit budget/time to a full rollout (new offer, ad spend, content push) with no proof it works.
technique: Test Campaigns Are Mandatory Risk Management (Hopkins Ch 15) + Key Every Ad (Ch 21)
exact_steps: Any question in advertising can be answered cheaply and finally by a test in a few towns. Rule: a $3,000-$5,000 test replaces a $500,000 mistake. Test scale generalizes: what a thousand customers do, a million will do. Protocol: run the offer/headline/sample variant in 1-2 local markets with KEYED tracking (unique URL, coupon code, or tracked link), measure cost per inquiry and cost per booked client, scale ONLY the winning variant. The largest advertiser Hopkins knew built 26 profitable product lines by testing one at a time. Unkeyed spend is money spent blindly. SNIPED application: before pushing a new offer tier or paid boost ($30/day desktop 10-mile LA), run a small keyed test, trace cost per booked Reset, scale only if it clears.
inputs_needed: Offer/headline variants, a keyed tracking mechanism (unique link/code), 1-2 test markets/audiences, budget cap for the test
output_artifact: Keyed test plan with cost-per-inquiry and cost-per-booked-client targets, scale/kill decision criteria
when_to_use: Before any new offer tier, paid boost, or content distribution push; quarterly when allocating budget
when_not: When the test itself would execute payment/outreach against the no-execute lock; for tiny reversible decisions where a test costs more than the mistake

problem: how to price, should I discount, cheap vs premium, race to the bottom, justify high price
symptom: Tempted to lower price to win a price-sensitive prospect, or worried the price is too high.
technique: Cheapness Repels; Price Signals Quality (Hopkins Ch 6 psychology levers)
exact_steps: Hopkins proved by keyed test: cheapness repels. People want to feel they can afford the best; a low price signals low quality and attracts the wrong buyer. Do NOT lower price to win price-sensitive prospects. SNIPED lock alignment: hold the Reset $1,500 floor; trade SCOPE, never price (decline cleanly or reduce deliverables, never cut the number). When a prospect pushes on price, reframe premium as the standard the best command, not a cost. Related lever: exclusivity ('offer limited to executives') outpulls the same offer to all, reinforcing premium identity.
inputs_needed: The current floor ($1,500 Reset), the prospect's stated budget objection, available scope levers (deliverable count, environments, turnaround)
output_artifact: A scope-flex counter that holds the price floor, plus reframe language positioning premium as the standard
when_to_use: Preparing a quote, responding to a budget objection, deciding whether to discount, Op Kit / Brand System pitch
when_not: Never below the $1,500 floor; do not use to justify gouging a good-fit client who can't reach scope (trade scope down instead)

problem: client hesitant to pay, lower risk for buyer, payment terms, deposit vs pay later, close friction
symptom: Prospect is interested but hesitant to commit money upfront; close stalls on the money step.
technique: Pay-Later / Pay-After-Proof Outperforms Refund Offers (Hopkins Ch 6, the horse story)
exact_steps: Hopkins' keyed result: 'come pay me then' (pay after you see the result) out-pulls 'come back for your money' (try-and-return-for-refund). Removing the buyer's upfront risk while keeping skin minimal beats a refund guarantee. SNIPED application: structure the close so proof precedes the bulk of payment where possible (deposit + balance on gallery delivery, or proof-frame before booking). This aligns directly with the SNIPED 'payment follows proof' lock: payment/entity structure follows proof, never blocks it. Use the fastest legit link/invoice once the prospect has seen value; never let the money mechanism block the sale.

technique: Research Before You Write (Hopkins Ch 11)
exact_steps: Never write copy before researching the consumer. Hopkins read entire medical libraries to find ONE scientific fact that became the Puffed Wheat campaign; surveyed 12,000 physicians, 1,000 men on shaving desires, 130 interviewers canvassing food preferences. The pork-and-beans canvass found 96% baked beans at home, so the winning campaign was about switching from home-baked, not brand-vs-brand, a discovery only research revealed. problem: free shoot, should I give free work, sample, lead magnet, who gets a discount, strategic free, giving away value
symptom: Tempted to scatter free shoots / free samples broadly to drum up interest, or unsure who should get free/trade work.
technique: Samples Must Be Earned, Not Scattered (Hopkins Ch 13)
exact_steps: Samples scattered to uninterested people are wasted and cheapen the product. Correct method: create desire and a mental impression FIRST through the offer, then give the sample only to people who demonstrate interest by some EFFORT (mailing a coupon, presenting it at a store). The sample then confirms expectations already set. Friction-data: a sample requested by mail cost 70 cents each; by store-coupon presentation only 18-22 cents, so make response friction-light but still require an effort signal. Never charge for a sample (the dime exceeds the price in lost responses). SNIPED application: Strategic Free / FreeCollab / Cultural Doc shoots go ONLY to people who have signaled interest and fit the scene-density/lineage criteria, never scattered for reach; the free work confirms the premium standard, it does not advertise availability.

technique: Key Every Ad; Measure Cost Per Customer (Hopkins Ch 21)
exact_steps: Hopkins saw advertisers spending $700,000/year not knowing if advertising worked at all. The only questions that matter: cost per customer ACQUIRED and revenue per customer over time. Unkeyed ads are money spent blindly; every campaign needs a mechanism to trace returns. Scientific advertising is impossible without instrumentation. Money-path scoring: rank channels/openers by cost-per-booked-client and revenue-per-client; kill the unkeyed and the unprofitable. problem: prospect interaction priority, should I pitch, free pitch, what's my goal with this lead

technique: 4-Priority Hierarchy for new business
exact_steps: Rank every prospect interaction by this fixed priority order: 1) Win Without Pitching (close via conversation, no free pitch). 2) Derail the Pitch (if a pitch/free-proposal process is forming, redirect it to a conversation). 3) Gain the Inside Track (if you must compete, get positioned as the frontrunner). 4) Walk Away. Companion rule: 'No is the second best answer' and you want to hear it EARLY (lowers cost of sale). Selling = respectful facilitation, NOT persuasion. The 3-step facilitation model matches the buying cycle: help the unaware (thought leadership) -> inspire the interested (portfolio/examples) -> reassure the intent (process/methodology/phased entry, NOT free proposals).

problem: how to write a proposal, proposal template, should I send a deck, overinvesting in proposals

technique: Words Not Paper: proposal is a contract, not a sales tool

The written proposal only CONFIRMS the verbal yes already reached; it is never the persuasion vehicle. Overinvesting in proposals signals need, creates buying resistance, and makes 'no' harder to hear. RULE: if the deal is complex enough to require real pre-engagement work to even scope it, charge for a diagnostic phase (paid discovery). Doctors charge for MRIs; you charge for diagnostics. For SNIPED: do not build elaborate free decks; close in conversation, then send a short confirming doc.

symptom: finding out late the client can't afford you, money never discussed, wasted sales time
technique: Address Money Early: Minimum Level of Engagement (MLE)
exact_steps: Rule: 'Those who cannot talk about money do not make it.' Set a Minimum Level of Engagement (MLE) = roughly 10% of your annual TARGET fee income, and share it EARLY. MLE is a FILTER, not an ultimatum. You may reserve the right to waive it, but waiving it without ever mentioning it = failure to use it. Lean-into-money line: 'I'm a little concerned about whether an organization your size can afford us.' Walking away faster lowers the cost of sale. For SNIPED: the $1,500 Reset floor is the price floor; MLE-style money-early qualification screens fit BEFORE diagnosis. Trade scope, never price.

problem: client wants a discount, how to handle price pushback, loss leader, lower my price

technique: Refuse to Work at a Loss: discount alternatives + discount discipline
exact_steps: No loss leaders. Profit margin is HIGHEST in phases 1-2 (diagnose/prescribe) and only diminishes; 'start cheap and build' is a fantasy. Discount alternatives IN ORDER before ever cutting price: (1) offer guarantees on phase 1, (2) offer favorable payment terms, (3) hold ground. If you must discount, it is (a) a LAST resort, only after ALL other objections are cleared, gated by the line 'If we agreed to this price, is there anything else stopping us from moving forward?' and (b) you MUST document the discount explicitly in writing so the client cannot reset the baseline. SNIPED lock: trade scope, not price; the $1,500 floor holds.

problem: how to write offer copy / feature vs benefit / why should they care / value clusters
symptom: Copy lists features (compositing, 5-pass cull) without translating to what the client achieves; buyer can't connect to their goal
technique: Feature > Benefit > Value Chain, reduce to 1-4 value clusters
exact_steps: For each provable attribute, run the chain: Feature (what it is) → Benefit (what it does) → Value (what it enables for the customer in THEIR goals). Then collapse all value into 1-4 value clusters maximum. More than 4 dilutes. Offer copy leads with the value cluster, supports with benefit, footnotes the feature. Example shape: Feature = AI-defended identity-locked composite world; Benefit = founder appears in editorial scenes impossible to shoot live; Value = scene-density status signal that closes premium clients.

output_artifact: 1-4 value clusters with feature→benefit→value mapping

problem: good fit client / bad fit client / who to target / ideal client / lead screening
symptom: Chasing broad audience; deals stall, prospects haggle price, churn, low referrals
technique: Best-Fit Customer Definition (component 4) as a 4-signal screen
exact_steps: Define best-fit by 4 behavioral signals, not demographics: (1) buys fast, (2) never asks for a discount, (3) refers others, (4) would fight you if you tried to take the product away. Score each inbound lead against these 4. A lead hitting 3-4 = pursue at Reset floor $1,500. A lead that haggles price (fails signal 2) or stalls (fails signal 1) = likely poor-fit; do not lower price, flex scope or decline cleanly. Start NARROW (e.g., editorial brand photography for LA founders), broaden only with evidence. Broader targeting reduces close rates, increases churn, attracts poor-fit buyers.
inputs_needed: Lead behavior observations, current niche definition
output_artifact: Best-fit scorecard (4 signals) + pursue/flex/decline decision
when_to_use: On every new inbound lead before booking a discovery call or VIB push
when_not: Do not broaden the target just to fill the pipeline; do not drop the $1,500 floor for a fast-but-haggling lead

problem: how to position against competitors / niche down / market category / dominate a segment
symptom: Competing head-to-head against all photographers; no clear reason a buyer picks SNIPED
technique: Big Fish, Small Pond positioning style (best path for small players)
exact_steps: Pick one of 3 styles: (a) Head to Head (claim best for all buyers, only viable if you are leader or no leader exists), (b) Big Fish Small Pond (dominate a subsegment with distinct unmet needs), (c) Create a New Game (define a new category, hardest, needs market shift + education + capital + 'why now'). For SNIPED, default to Big Fish Small Pond: dominate 'editorial brand photography for LA founders'. The subsegment must pass 3 tests: identifiable, big enough to hit revenue goals, has a need the category leader structurally CANNOT serve well. If any test fails, narrow or pick a different pond.
inputs_needed: Candidate subsegment, revenue target, leader's structural weaknesses
output_artifact: Chosen positioning style + 3-test pass/fail for the subsegment
when_to_use: Quarterly positioning review, lane decisions, new-offer launch
when_not: Do not pick Head to Head unless you are the leader; do not pick Create a New Game without capital and a clear why-now

problem: AI-powered framing / trend hook / new luxury / how to use a trend in copy
symptom: Copy leads with a trend ('AI-powered', 'new luxury') and confuses buyers about what SNIPED actually is
technique: Market Category First, Trend Second (Trend-First Gate)
exact_steps: State the market category (what you ARE) FIRST. Only then optionally layer a relevant trend (why this matters NOW). The trend must link directly and demonstrably to the market category and the product's value. Never lead with the trend as a substitute for the category. Gate: before publishing any copy using 'AI', 'editorial', or 'new luxury', confirm (1) the category is stated first, (2) the trend has a provable link to value. Trend-only framing fails the gate and gets rewritten.
inputs_needed: Stated market category, candidate trend, value link
output_artifact: Category-first copy with trend layered + gate pass/fail
when_to_use: Finalizing Carrd copy, captions, Op Kit, any copy invoking a trend
when_not: Do not drop the trend if it has no provable value link; cut it instead

problem: stuck on old positioning / how to reposition / default assumptions / can't see my offer clearly
symptom: Offer framing trapped in the product you set out to build; defaulting to old assumptions about what SNIPED is
technique: Positioning Baggage Rule (surface and kill the default first)
exact_steps: Before running any positioning work, explicitly NAME the current positioning assumptions in writing (e.g., 'SNIPED = a photographer', 'we sell sessions'). Founders are trapped in the product they set out to build. Surface each assumption, then deliberately KILL the default before starting the exercise. This unlocks better options (consistent with the possibility-engine lock: identity emerges from proof, not from the default you started with).

output_artifact: Named-and-killed positioning-baggage list
when_to_use: Start of any repositioning, new-offer, or quarterly positioning review
when_not: Do not skip; skipping bakes the old default into the new positioning

problem: how to build my positioning / positioning process / offer build from scratch
symptom: No repeatable procedure; positioning done as a one-line statement that never gets used
technique: 10-Step Positioning Workshop (sequenced procedure)
exact_steps: Run in order: (1) List best-fit customers. (2) Form a small cross-functional team (for solo SNIPED: pull in assistant/contractor perspectives). (3) Surface and name current positioning baggage. (4) List true competitive alternatives from customer POV. (5) List unique attributes vs those alternatives. (6) Map attributes to 1-4 value themes. (7) Identify who cares most about that value. (8) Choose market frame (Head to Head / Big Fish Small Pond / Create a New Game). (9) Optionally layer a relevant trend. (10) Capture in a positioning canvas PLUS a full detailed document. Then build the sales story arc and write the master messaging doc. Output is documents, never a one-line statement.
inputs_needed: Best-fit list, alternatives, attributes, value themes, chosen style
output_artifact: Positioning canvas + detailed positioning document
when_to_use: Building or rebuilding a SNIPED offer (Reset, Op Kit, Brand System)
when_not: Do not substitute a Positioning Statement template; it is condemned as useless

problem: how to pitch / sales deck structure / discovery call script / pitch flow
symptom: Pitch jumps straight to product/features; no problem setup, buyer doesn't feel the gap
technique: Sales Story Arc (6-beat pitch structure)
exact_steps: Structure every pitch/discovery as a 6-beat arc: (1) Problem definition. (2) Gaps in current solutions (the competitive alternatives). (3) The 'perfect world' (what good looks like). (4) Product intro framed by the chosen market category. (5) Value themes (your 1-4 clusters). (6) Call to action. Replace slide-presentations with this conversation arc. Diagnose the problem before prescribing the product. Lands cleanly inside SNIPED's discovery-to-close: arc beats 1-3 = diagnose, beats 4-6 = prescribe.
inputs_needed: Competitive alternatives, market category, value clusters, the CTA (e.g., book Reset)
output_artifact: 6-beat sales story script for pitch/discovery
when_to_use: Discovery calls, Op Kit pitch, proposal narrative, VIB follow-up framing
when_not: Do not open with product/features; do not skip the problem and gap beats

problem: copy drifts / inconsistent messaging / brand voice baseline / messaging document
symptom: Every new piece of copy reinvents the language; offer descriptions drift off-positioning
technique: Master Messaging Document (anti-drift baseline)
exact_steps: After positioning is set, write ONE master messaging document as the baseline so all downstream copy (captions, Carrd, Op Kit, DMs, LinkedIn) references it instead of drifting. It contains: market category statement, the 1-4 value clusters, provable attributes with proof, and the approved phrase bank. Every new copy artifact must trace back to this doc. Review/update it on the 6-month positioning cadence. Pairs with the existing SNIPED positioning-phrase bank.
inputs_needed: Finished positioning (category, value clusters, provable attributes, phrase bank)
output_artifact: Master messaging document (single source of truth)
when_to_use: Immediately after positioning workshop; reference before writing any copy
when_not: Do not write downstream copy before this baseline exists

problem: how to price / what to charge / pricing signal / premium pricing justification
symptom: Pricing set independent of positioning; premium price feels unjustified or buyer expects commodity rate
technique: Pricing Reinforces Positioning (niche = premium expected)
exact_steps: Let price be a positioning SIGNAL, not just a number. In a specialized/niche category, niche/premium pricing is EXPECTED by the buyer and reinforces the category. A specialist who prices like a generalist contradicts their own positioning and confuses buyers. So: once you choose Big Fish Small Pond (specialist), hold premium pricing as category-consistent. Honors SNIPED locks: Reset floor stays $1,500, trade scope not price. Dropping below floor would signal generalist/commodity positioning and undercut the category. If budget is short, flex scope, never the price signal.
inputs_needed: Chosen market category/style, current price, the $1,500 floor
output_artifact: Price-as-signal check (consistent / contradicts positioning)
when_to_use: Preparing a quote, considering a discount, Op Kit / Brand System pricing
when_not: Do not discount below floor to win a haggler; that breaks the category signal

source_segment: doctrine: Execution - pricing reinforces positioning (niche/premium expected)

problem: when to revisit positioning / positioning review cadence / market changed / competitor entered
symptom: Positioning set once and never revisited; drifts as market/competition/tech shifts
technique: Positioning Review Trigger (6-month cadence + event triggers)
exact_steps: Review positioning every 6 months OR immediately when a trigger fires: a major competitor enters, a regulation changes, or a new technology shifts buyer assumptions. On any trigger, restart at Step 4 (re-list competitive alternatives from customer POV) and re-run the downstream chain (attributes → value → category → trend → messaging). For SNIPED specifically, any major AI-tooling shift is a tech trigger that forces re-running the alternatives list.
inputs_needed: Last review date, list of market/competitor/tech/regulatory events since
output_artifact: Review decision (hold vs re-run from Step 4) + updated canvas if changed
when_to_use: Quarterly cockpit / Constraint Audit, or on any market-shift event
when_not: Do not skip a scheduled review just because nothing 'feels' different
